# A test drives a datepicker on every target: `c.d.change(day)`
# commits a date, which the `:value` binding writes back.
#
# Each target's datepicker is an input with a value a test can put there:
# html's date input, gtk4's GtkCalendar (the invoker selects the day, then
# fires day-selected), fyne's DateEntry, bubbletea's tui.DateInput (a
# YYYY-MM-DD text field), android's SnglDateField and the interpreter's own.
# bubbletea and fyne used to render a label, which nothing could drive.
#
# gtk4's override names its calendar `#cal` for the effect that selects the
# bound date, and the call site names it `#d`: the effect's read of `cal`
# follows the node to the call site's handle, or it named a field nothing
# builds.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import time "sngl:time"

component picker node {
    var picked option[time.date] = null
    datepicker #d(:value=picked)
}

func testPick(t Test, c picker) {
    var day time.date = "2024-03-05"
    c.d.change(day)
    t.assert(c.picked == day)
}
